svg.title: MailStorm detailed architecture atlas
svg.desc: Implemented architecture, route inventory, database schema, worker recovery, security, deployment, limits and system design references.
svg.text: READ TOP → BOTTOM • Flow → API details → data & workers → safeguards → references
Browser popup → API code exchange + userinfo. Worker refreshes
tokens server-side. Google credentials never become the browser
Browser → signed S3 incoming object. API → sealed snapshot. Worker ←
streamed CSV. Development uses API PUT + local files.
Worker ↔ database for claims and outcomes. Browser ← status/result
polling. Closing the tab does not stop the job; Cancel requests it
PRODUCTION PATH ABOVE • LOCAL SWAP: SQLite + local files + embedded worker • Arrows show logical flow, not a separate message broker.
React 19 • React Router 7 • Tailwind • React Scripts.
Login, protected email form, legacy callback redirect, and privacy
CSV drag/drop; TXT or HTML template; Process Files; manual
Subject/body editing, Send, Cancel, Reset, dark mode, Sign Out,
AuthContext + session.js hold profile and opaque app session in
useEmailSending resumes a running job on mount; only the
Reset forgets the batch identity and permits an intentional new
Origin allowlist + X-Requested-With verification; code length
Code exchange runs in a thread; Google userinfo supplies the
Owner = SHA-256(Google sub). Existing refresh token is retained
if Google omits a new one.
Fernet encrypts provider tokens, expiry, name and email on the
Browser receives a separate random app token; DB stores its
FastAPI / Uvicorn; Pydantic request validation; CORS permits
Protected routes resolve owner before reading request bodies.
ASGI middleware counts incoming bytes without buffering the
Content-Length rejection, receive deadline 120 s, and at most 8
active POST/PUT requests per API process.
Body caps depend on route; CSV exact size and content limits are
POST /v1/uploads {size, sha256} → 201 with upload ID and
Local: PUT /v1/uploads/{id}/content; streaming write, exclusive file
Production: browser POSTs file directly to a signed S3 URL, with
no app bearer token sent to S3.
Local states: reserved → receiving → received → finalizing →
S3 states: reserved → finalizing → uploaded. Transitions require
Failed uploads require a new reservation. Admission: 20
UUID Idempotency-Key required. DB unique(owner, key) makes
key/content returns existing ID; changed content → 409.
POST /v1/campaigns/{id}/cancel sets a durable flag. An in-flight
invalid inputs require a new campaign.
POST /send-emails keeps legacy multipart field names but returns
202 JSON, not the old SSE stream.
GET /v1/campaigns → latest 50 campaigns for the current owner.
GET /v1/campaigns/{id}/logs streams CSV in 250-row pages and
GET /ping is liveness; GET /readyz verifies DB connectivity and
Readiness does not verify worker liveness, S3 access, or Gmail
original CSV is a local file.
Production: boto3 S3 client; private bucket supplied by the
operator; signed POST valid for 900 s.
Signed policy binds object size and AES256 server-side
HEAD checks size; conditional COPY captures the ETag snapshot
Browser can overwrite only its incoming target; worker reads the
S3 checksum is validated by the importer before any sending.
Storage client: 5 s connect, 30 s read, bounded retries. Cleanup
SQLAlchemy Core + psycopg/PostgreSQL in production; SQLite
job_connections: hashed owner PK, encrypted Google
job_sessions: hashed token PK, owner FK, expiry.
job_uploads: ID, owner, size, SHA-256, state, created time;
job_campaigns: owner FK + upload FK, idempotency
key/fingerprint, encrypted template, state and imported flag.
Campaign fields also hold counters, cancel flag, lease owner,
generation, lease expiry, next_at and error.
Only requested status columns are fetched for status/list APIs;
state, attempt count, provider ID and error.
job_attempts: attempt ID, campaign FK, row number, state,
provider ID, error and creation time.
Campaign deletion cascades to recipients and attempts.
job_scheduler: singleton row holding project next_at and the
job_schema: initial version 1. Migration creates job_* tables;
Indexes cover owner/key uniqueness, due jobs, owner leases,
recipient state/row, retention and session/upload lookup.
PostgreSQL pool: 8 connections + 8 overflow per process, 5 s pool
Worker streams UTF-8/BOM CSV through a 64 KiB limited reader;
At most 32 unique normalized columns; name + email required;
Quoted CSV supported; malformed rows/encoding, unsafe names
or invalid addresses reject the campaign.
First name is used for personalization; supported placeholders are
Unknown placeholders and unsafe/oversized subjects rejected;
Expanded body limits checked without building every full message.
Encrypted recipient rows written in chunks of 250. Sending starts
only after the entire import succeeds.
Dedicated asyncio worker uses a UUID identity; idle polling interval
Claim oldest eligible due campaign; one leased campaign per
owner; at most 8 across all workers.
Each claim increments generation. Lease lasts 120 s; heartbeat
Worker mutations verify campaign ID, worker ID, generation and
live lease; stale writes raise LostLease.
Expired leases recovered in groups of 50; unfinished submitting
One import or one recipient attempt per claim; release schedules
SIGTERM/SIGINT stops new claims and allows the current
Refresh Google access token when expiry is within 60 s; version
check prevents overwriting a newer login.
Record recipient + attempt as submitting before contacting Gmail.
Personalize; build UTF-8 MIME EmailMessage in a thread;
base64url encode; httpx POST to Gmail messages.send.
Default send deadline 30 s. Success stores provider message ID
Connect/pool failures and explicit rate-limit rejection can retry; max
Read/write uncertainty and 5xx become unknown; provider errors
Campaign happy path: importing → queued → running → queued
Other campaign states: retry_wait, awaiting_auth, blocked, invalid
Retry and lease recovery never automatically replay accepted or
Explicit ambiguous provider errors pause; crash recovery can
Unique campaign creation prevents duplicate jobs for one key; it is
Fencing protects DB writes only. Gmail cannot enforce the
generation. Accepted is not inbox delivery; exactly-once is not
Default input: CSV 2 MiB / 500 recipients; subject 998 characters;
Active queue caps: 10 campaigns per owner, 1,000 overall.
DB timestamps share sender pacing (1.1 s) and project pacing
Rate-limit responses defer the sender; project rate-limit reason can
Retry-After supports seconds/date; delay is capped at 24 h.
PostgreSQL clock supplies scheduling/lease time; SQLite uses
No network or file parsing inside DB transactions; the global
scheduler lock still limits write throughput.
Papa Parse processes CSV in 256 KiB chunks; preview validation
Incremental SHA-256 hashes file slices; browser stores batch
fingerprint + UUID for 24 h in sessionStorage.
Send flow: reserve → transfer → seal → create → poll. Status
Result cursor advances over terminal recipient rows. Transient
polling failures back off up to 30 s, with 6 retries.
API fetch deadline 45 s; local PUT 120 s. Direct S3 upload relies
Unmount aborts observation; server work continues. Cancel
CSV export is streamed by the API but collected as a Blob in the
browser; very large downloads still use browser memory.
Fernet encrypts recipient data, templates and Google credentials;
Client secret and encryption key stay server-side. Browser app
token remains accessible to same-origin scripts.
Production requires HTTPS frontend origins, PostgreSQL, S3 and
Development generates a private encryption.key file; keep it with
Worker cleanup runs roughly every 60 s. Terminal/paused
campaigns expire after 30 days by default.
Per pass: up to 25 campaigns, 1,000 sessions and 250 orphan
Unreferenced uploads age out after 1 h; objects are deleted
before upload metadata. Idle credentials expire once no
Local: one API process + embedded worker, SQLite, local files;
Production: separate API and worker processes share
PostgreSQL, S3 configuration and the same encryption key.
API lifespan creates shared httpx client, Store and Objects; worker
Run python -m backend.jobs.migrate before production startup;
Render blueprint defines paid API, worker and database; frontend
S3_BUCKET/AWS identity and Google OAuth secrets.
S3 bucket, CORS, TLS proxy, backups, key rotation and alerts
Latest local checks: 37 backend + 40 frontend tests passed; build
10,000-row late-error test confirms 250-row imports and zero
Tests cover ownership, duplicate creation, lease takeover,
recovery, quota deferral, refresh and UI workflows.
PostgreSQL integration is wired to a CI service but was skipped
No live Gmail/S3 capacity certification. Edge rate limits,
worker-health monitoring and dashboards are not provisioned.
Legacy batch_store.py is not the current send path. Old hash-only
Drain/reconcile legacy sends, migrate, deploy API + UI together
and sign in again. No Redis, Celery, Kafka or WebSocket layer is
These are pattern mappings from the code review, not claims of full compliance or evidence that the repository authors cited these sources.
202 returns a durable ID; the browser polls status while workers run
